title: A Window into Bond Investors’ Uncertainty About R-Star - Liberty Street Economics
gist: A New York Fed Staff Report models bond pricing under incomplete information and finds investors' perceived r-star has been remarkably stable between 0 and 2.5 percent from the 1960s to 2022, with 95 percent uncertainty bands of ±170 basis points that barely narrow even with full hindsight (±130bp). The late-sample rise in r-star is more modest than other term-structure estimates suggest, casting doubt on the death of the low-r-star era.

themes.theme: Investor-perceived r-star is stable, not rising

insights.claim: A New York Fed bond-pricing model finds investors' perceived r-star trend followed a remarkably stable path between 0 percent and 2.5 percent from the 1960s through 2022, with no regime break at the end of the sample.
insights.speaker: Guillaume Roussellet
insights.so_what: If the market-implied equilibrium real rate never actually left its historical 0-2.5% band, term premium and cyclical policy — not a higher r-star — explain elevated long-end yields.
insights.quote: which shows a remarkably stable path from the 1960s to 2022 between 0 percent and 2.5 percent

insights.claim: Once investor information frictions are modeled, the late-sample rise in r-star is more modest and gradual than other financial-market and term-structure estimates imply, casting doubt on the claim that the low-r-star era has ended.
insights.speaker: Guillaume Roussellet
insights.so_what: A direct challenge to the 'higher for longer neutral rate' consensus — bearish for the structural-steepener/higher-terminal-rate thesis in long-duration Treasuries.
insights.quote: also casts doubt on the death of the low r-star era
insights.locator: Beyond parameters that are estimated on

insights.claim: The model's r-star estimates are smoother and less volatile than the Laubach-Williams (2003) series published on the New York Fed's website, while aligning with the yield-curve-based Bauer and Rudebusch (2020) estimates.
insights.speaker: Guillaume Roussellet
insights.so_what: Which r-star series you anchor to materially changes the implied policy gap; yield-curve-based measures move far less than the widely quoted Laubach-Williams estimate.
insights.locator: Our estimates are in line with Bauer

themes.theme: The uncertainty bands swamp the signal

insights.claim: Investors' 95 percent confidence band around r-star is estimated at plus or minus 170 basis points, a range wider than most policy debates about the neutral rate.
insights.speaker: Guillaume Roussellet
insights.so_what: Any trade premised on a precise neutral-rate level is inside the noise band; fade strong r-star narratives and size rate positions to that uncertainty.
insights.quote: we also estimate investors’ 95 percent confidence bands of r-star at ±170 basis points

insights.claim: Estimated 95 percent confidence bands for the trend components are plus or minus 225 basis points for the nominal rate trend i-star, plus or minus 125 basis points for the inflation trend pi-star, and plus or minus 80 basis points for the growth trend.
insights.speaker: Guillaume Roussellet
insights.so_what: Uncertainty is concentrated in the nominal rate trend rather than growth, so long-end rate risk is dominated by unknowable policy-anchor drift.

insights.claim: At the end of the 2022 sample, investors' perceived nominal rate trend i-star sits at 3.75 percent but with a 95 percent band spanning 1.55 percent to 5.95 percent.
insights.speaker: Guillaume Roussellet
insights.so_what: A 440bp span on the anchor for long-run nominal rates justifies structurally wide long-end term premia and rich optionality on rates vol.
insights.quote: i-star is estimated at 3.75 percent by investors, with a 95 percent confidence band of [1.55 percent, 5.95 percent]

insights.claim: Even with full hindsight over 1960-2022, two-sided r-star estimates still carry uncertainty bands of plus or minus 130 basis points, showing that the ambiguity around the neutral rate barely shrinks with more data.
insights.speaker: Guillaume Roussellet
insights.so_what: Waiting for data to resolve the neutral-rate debate is futile — the irreducible uncertainty is a permanent feature to be priced, not a temporary fog.
insights.quote: uncertainty bands are still as wide as ±130 basis points, reflecting the high degree of uncertainty surrounding r-star even with look-ahead bias

insights.claim: The framework assumes macro aggregates are driven by long-run trends plus shorter-lived cycles that investors cannot disentangle in real time, so they form an optimal but imperfect trend-cycle decomposition from aggregates plus private information.
insights.speaker: Guillaume Roussellet
insights.so_what: A reusable lens: yields price beliefs about trend versus cycle, so surprises come from belief revisions rather than from data itself.

insights.claim: Bond yields reflect investors' perceived trend and cycle components rather than the true unobservable states, meaning the term structure can only ever reveal what investors themselves can see.
insights.speaker: Guillaume Roussellet
insights.so_what: Market-implied macro signals are a read on consensus perception, not on truth — useful as a positioning gauge, dangerous as a forecast.
insights.quote: the term structure of interest rates can only reveal the information that investors can see
insights.locator: One general mechanism emerges from this

insights.claim: Policymakers can only learn something new from the yield curve to the extent that investors hold information the policymakers do not already have.
insights.speaker: Guillaume Roussellet
insights.so_what: Frames when Fed reaction functions should respond to market pricing versus ignore it — relevant for anticipating policy sensitivity to bond selloffs.
insights.quote: policymakers can learn from them as long as investors possess different information than the policymakers
insights.locator: One general mechanism emerges from this

insights.claim: The model defines r-star in finance terms as the spread between the nominal interest rate trend and the inflation trend, with investors observing only the interest rate, inflation and growth plus a private signal about the long run.
insights.speaker: Guillaume Roussellet
insights.so_what: Gives a replicable way to back out a market-implied real neutral rate directly from nominal trend minus inflation trend rather than from output-gap models.
insights.locator: A Bond Pricing Model in Incomplete Information

themes.theme: Policy stance was tighter than it felt

insights.claim: Ex post two-sided estimates put investors' r-star during the Great Moderation below the real-time perceived level, implying monetary policy was more restrictive at the time than market participants believed.
insights.speaker: Guillaume Roussellet
insights.so_what: Historical precedent that the perceived policy stance is systematically revised toward 'tighter' — a bias worth applying to current assessments of restrictiveness.
insights.quote: investors’ estimated r-star during the great moderation is lower ex post than in real time, reflecting an ex post evaluation of the monetary policy stance as being more restrictive than perceived at the time

insights.claim: The paper's policy prescription is that financial-market-based r-star estimates should never be used without accompanying uncertainty measures, since investor uncertainty does not decay over time.
insights.speaker: Guillaume Roussellet
insights.so_what: Signals a Fed research direction toward wider stated uncertainty around neutral, which supports higher structural rate volatility and less forward-guidance precision.
insights.quote: policymakers should consider financial-based estimates of r-star with accompanying uncertainty measures
